subject: Service assurance: deviation, remedy credits, and license scale path
messages:
From: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@luminabank.com>, LuminaBank Procurement <procure@luminabank.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: increased tail latency and Q2 impact — renewal conversation

Hi Sean,

We ran into two production incidents last week where token-level tail latency spiked above our SLA thresholds (both on the hosted API). The attached CSV has the per-hour tail 99.9% numbers for the last six weeks. Those spikes caused delayed responses for several live customer journeys and one customer escalation.

We’ve been happy with Redwood overall but given the operational impact and our upcoming contract renewal in August we need to discuss remedies, credits, and what a commercially viable path to predictable capacity looks like (dedicated vs premium tiers). Can we get a proposal that includes:

- A short remediation plan (engineering actions + timeline)
- Proposed make-good/credit treatment for the incidents
- Options and pricing for a predictable dedicated or premium onramp (pilot scope)

Cc’ing procurement (for timing). We’d like a concrete proposal by May 27 if possible.

Thanks,
Clara Zhao
Head of Platform Ops
LuminaBank

Attachments: lumina_latency_q2_summary.csv
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: increased tail latency and Q2 impact — renewal conversation

Clara — thanks for the heads up and for the data. I’m sorry to hear this caused customer impact. We take these incidents seriously.

Action plan from Redwood:
1) Immediate remediation: Karthik and the reliability team will run a hot-fix and KV cache tuning tomorrow morning to reduce observed tail spikes; we’ll monitor and share an initial report within 24 hours.
2) Make-good: We’ll propose a one-time service credit for the impacted windows, and a short-term SLO uplift (short-run higher priority routing) while we stabilize.
3) Predictable capacity path: Marcus will put together a dedicated pilot offer (3-week pilot, guaranteed throughput, limited burst) and an alternative premium SLA addendum with price/commit terms.

I’ve looped Marcus and Grace to own the commercial proposal and pilot scope. Expect the proposal doc + addendum draft by EOD May 27.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: increased tail latency and Q2 impact — remediation items

Clara/Sean — quick update from the reliability squad.

What we saw: the tail latency correlates with a small subset of customers sending long-context generative requests during batch windows; our auto-batching configuration allowed some requests to queue and exceed the target SLO. Root cause appears to be a combination of (a) sequence length spikes, (b) suboptimal KV cache warm-up for this workload pattern, and (c) an edge-case in the kernel selection for the model variant you’re using.

Immediate steps (today -> 48h):
- Deploy KV cache warm-up to reduce cache misses (hotfix)
- Apply a tighter per-customer batching cap for LuminaBank’s tenant
- Swap to a compatible model variant with lower tail characteristics for peak windows (no quality regression expected; we’ll A/B check)

We’ll ship logs and a preliminary mitigation report in the next 24 hours. For the pilot: suggested scope is a 3-week dedicated capacity pilot with 2x headroom and a follow-up performance validation.

—Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_scope_draft.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>, LuminaBank Procurement <procure@luminabank.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed commercial remediation + pilot options (DEAL-8372)

Clara / Lumina procurement — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short commercial package:

- Proposed credits: 10% service credit for the impacted billing month (applied to July invoice) + a one-time stability credit equal to one week of average hosted usage during the incident windows.
- Pilot option A (Dedicated pilot): 3-week dedicated pool, 2x tested headroom, 1% introductory pricing uplift, Redundancy SLA for pilot window, implementation support included.
- Pilot option B (Premium onramp addendum): No dedicated hardware; priority routing and tighter SLOs with a 6-month term and a higher per-token rate but cheaper than long-term dedicated.
- Contract mechanics: addendum draft attached (rdwd_proposed_addendum_v1.pdf) + DocuSign pathway for signature.

We recommend Pilot A for fastest predictable results; Pilot B is viable if procurement prefers not to add dedicated infrastructure. If you want, we can structure a credit-for-commitment trade: agree a 12-month higher-tier commitment and receive additional service credits and a preferential SLA.

Request: could you confirm procurement timing? If you can accept the pilot scope and a PO by June 4 we’ll prioritize onboarding.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdwd_proposed_addendum_v1.pdf
From: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, LuminaBank Procurement <procure@luminabank.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed commercial remediation + pilot options (DEAL-8372)

Thanks Marcus — received and shared internally. High level response from Lumina: we’re supportive of a short dedicated pilot to validate stability, but procurement wants clarity on the credit math and an explicit rollback clause if pilot fails to meet SLOs. Also need a statement that pilot telemetry will be accessible to our ops team.

Requesting: a short addendum that covers
- Exact credit calculation example (how the two credits stack)
- Rollback/exit mechanics at pilot end (30-day evaluation and defined failure triggers)
- Telemetry access (read-only dashboards and sampling logs)

If you can send a revised addendum with those items, procurement will aim to sign the pilot PO by June 3.

Regards,
Clara
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@luminabank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, LuminaBank Procurement <procure@luminabank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed commercial remediation + pilot options (DEAL-8372)

Clara — appreciate the clarity and the quick internal alignment. We’ll get a revised addendum that explicitly calls out the credit calculation worked example, rollback triggers, and telemetry access.

Next steps:
- Marcus and legal will update the addendum today and circulate a redline + clean copy.
- Karthik will publish a preliminary mitigation report and a telemetry endpoint for Lumina ops to consume (read-only) by EOD tomorrow.
- We’ll aim to have the PO-ready package to you by June 1 to meet your June 3 procurement target.

If it helps, here’s the DocuSign start link for the current draft (will be updated with redlines): https://docusign.redwood.com/start/DEAL-8372

—Sean
